user.title: Main fuse
user.description: Describe the main fuse that all your loads share.

data_description.voltage: Used to convert between watts and amps. 230 V in most of Europe, 120 V in North America.
data_description.fuse_a: The rating of your main fuse, for example 16, 20 or 25 A.

sources.title: Main fuse sensors
sources.description: Pick the sensor that measures each phase at the main fuse ({phases}): current in A, or power in W. For example from a P1/HAN port, a Shelly Pro 3EM or a load balancer.

error.unsupported_unit: This sensor must report A, mA, W or kW.
error.same_sensor_twice: Use a different sensor for each phase.

abort.already_configured: This main fuse is already set up.

create_entry.default:
The main fuse is set up. Next, add your loads with **Add load** on the HA Phase Map entry.

To use the dashboard card, **reload the browser** first (Ctrl+Shift+R, or in the companion app Settings → Companion app → Debugging → Reset frontend cache): *Phase Bus Card* only appears in the card picker after a reload.

init.title: Options
init.description: Overload warning, and labels that show which phase each load's device is on.

data.margin_a: Warning margin below the fuse rating

data_description.margin_a: The overload sensor turns on when a phase gets this close to the fuse rating.
data_description.overload_delay_s: How long the phase must stay that high before the warning turns on.

phase_labels.name: Phase labels on devices
phase_labels.description: Puts a label such as "Fas: 2" on the device of every load's meter, so you can see and filter by phase anywhere in Home Assistant. A device that measures several phases gets one label per phase. Labels follow when a load moves.

data_description.label_name: Free text, for example Fas or Inkommande fas. The label reads "name: value".

disable_labels.title: Labels set by HA Phase Map
disable_labels.description: HA Phase Map has added {labels} phase labels to {devices} devices. Remove them, or keep them? Labels you set yourself are never touched.

menu_options.keep_labels: Keep them (HA Phase Map stops managing them)

error.empty_value: Every phase needs a label value.
error.same_value_twice: Use a different label value for each phase.

options.equal: Split equally over the connected phases

user.title: Add a load
user.description: What kind of load is it?

menu_options.multi: A multi-phase load with one meter per phase

meter.title: Load with one meter
meter.description: Pick the sensor that measures this load (power or current). Next you can place it behind another meter, and then pick its phase with a suggestion based on the last 10 days.

phase.title: Which phase?
phase.description: {name} is probably on **{phase}** ({confidence} confidence: {steps} on/off steps, gain {gain}). Change it if you know better.

data.portable: Portable: follow it when it moves to another phase

data_description.portable: For something that is moved between sockets (a space heater, a kettle). HA Phase Map watches its switch-on and switch-off events; when they clearly show another phase, it moves the load there by itself. Otherwise it asks under Settings → Repairs.
data_description.connected_phases: Only for a multi-phase load measured by one meter, such as a CEE outlet or a charger measured as a total. Pick the other phases it is wired to: it is then drawn as a multi-phase load and not checked for moves.
data_description.draw: With more than one phase: all of the meter's power on the phase above (a 1-phase car on a 3-phase charger), or split equally over the connected phases.

phase_manual.title: Which phase?
phase_manual.description: History could not tell which phase {name} is on ({steps} usable on/off steps in the last 10 days). Pick the phase, or come back after it has been switched on and off a few times.

data.portable: Portable: follow it when it moves to another phase

data_description.portable: For something that is moved between sockets (a space heater, a kettle). HA Phase Map watches its switch-on and switch-off events; when they clearly show another phase, it moves the load there by itself. Otherwise it asks under Settings → Repairs.
data_description.connected_phases: Only for a multi-phase load measured by one meter, such as a CEE outlet or a charger measured as a total. Pick the other phases it is wired to: it is then drawn as a multi-phase load and not checked for moves.
data_description.draw: With more than one phase: all of the meter's power on the phase above (a 1-phase car on a 3-phase charger), or split equally over the connected phases.

multi.title: Multi-phase load
multi.description: Pick the meter channel for each phase the load uses, for example the three phases of a Shelly Pro 3EM. Leave unused phases empty.

estimated.title: Load without a meter
estimated.description: Drawn with a dashed outline. Add a detector to notice when it runs.

data.name: Name
data.portable: Portable: follow it when it moves to another phase

data_description.portable: For something that is moved between sockets (a space heater, a kettle). HA Phase Map watches its switch-on and switch-off events; when they clearly show another phase, it moves the load there by itself. Otherwise it asks under Settings → Repairs.

parent.title: Measured by another meter?
parent.description: Is {name} downstream of another meter you have added, for example the meter on the garage's incoming cable? Then it is subtracted from that meter instead of the main fuse, and that meter shows what is left. Pre-selected from the Energy dashboard's upstream device when it has one.

reconfigure_meter.title: Edit load
reconfigure_meter.description: One meter. To make it a multi-phase load (for example a 3-phase charger that today only charges on one phase), pick the other phases under Also connected to.

data.name: Name
data.portable: Portable: follow it when it moves to another phase

data_description.connected_phases: Only for a multi-phase load measured by one meter, such as a CEE outlet or a charger measured as a total. Pick the other phases it is wired to: it is then drawn as a multi-phase load and not checked for moves.

error.unsupported_unit: This sensor must report A, mA, W or kW.
error.no_meter: Pick a meter for at least one phase.
error.outside_parent: The upstream meter does not measure every phase this load uses.

user.title: Unmetered load detector
user.description: Turns on when current that no meter explains rises on all the chosen phases at once, for example a sauna. Use it in automations, such as blocking a heat pump while the sauna runs.

data_description.min_current_a: Unmetered current above its normal level that counts as the load running. An 8 kW three-phase sauna adds about 11 A per phase.
data_description.off_delay_s: Keep the detector on this long after the current drops, so a thermostat switching on and off does not make it flicker.

confirm.title: Move {name} to {to}?
confirm.description:
When {name} switched on or off recently, the main fuse (or the meter it sits behind) changed on **{to}**, not on {from} where it is configured. It has probably been plugged into a socket on another phase.

Move it to {to}? If it is on {from} after all, ignore this repair instead.

abort.load_gone: The load no longer exists or is no longer a single-phase load.
